title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In these notes Grothendieck develops 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space. A tame stratified space X with poset of strata I is to be replaced by combinatorial-topological data. For each stratum i one has a compact piece Σ_i, morally the complement of an open tubular neighbourhood of the smaller strata in the closure of stratum i, a manifold with corners. The faces of these pieces are glued by 'link' fibrations. The previous page introduces (§10, item (29)) a topological space Σ_* with a partial order whose graph Σ_** ⊂ Σ_*×Σ_* is closed, and asks that pr_1 ('but', target) be an immersion. The present page makes this precise.

(25) There is a continuous map Σ_* → I, with I discrete, so Σ_* = ⊔_{i∈I} Σ_i. The order relation then splits as Σ_** = ⊔_{i≤j} Σ_ij, where Σ_ij = {(x,z) : x∈Σ_i, z∈Σ_j, x≤z}.

Condition (a). For all i≤j, the 'boundary' map Σ_ij → Σ_j, (x,z) ↦ z, is a 'cylindrical' closed embedding. Morally Σ_ij is the face of the manifold with corners Σ_j lying over stratum i. It has a collar, and its other projection Σ_ij → Σ_i is the link bundle. Consequence (25*): given z over j and i≤j, there is (at most) one x over i with x≤z. A marginal note rephrases this as a statement on the map Σ_{≤z} → I_{≤j}. The closed-embedding hypothesis also gives (26) Σ_ii = Σ_i: the order restricted to a fibre is trivial, since the diagonal is contained in Σ_ii, which embeds in Σ_i.

Condition (b), (27). Let Σ(n) be the space of strict flags (chains) x_0<…<x_n of length n in Σ_*. Mapping a chain to its sequence of strata gives Σ(n) → Drap_n(I), the strict flags of I. Hence Σ(n) = ⊔ Σ_{i_0…i_n} over strict flags i_0<…<i_n of I. In modern terms: the nerve of the topological poset Σ_* is a simplicial space fibred over the nerve of the discrete poset I. The pieces Σ_d are indexed by flags d of I.

The next page completes the axioms: (28) Σ_ijk = Σ_ik ∩ Σ_jk; disjointness of faces whose indices have no common lower bound; transversality of the faces Σ_ik inside Σ_k. These are exactly the axioms of a manifold with faces / corners whose faces are indexed by flags, i.e. an 'iterated fibration structure'.

Purpose. This axiomatizes the unfolded ('déployé') model of a stratified space, which the Esquisse d'un programme claims is equivalent to the tame stratified space. The mapping-cylinder constructions C_{Σ,d,d'} on the previous page re-glue X from these data.
errors: Condition (a) says Σ_ij → Σ_j is a closed embedding. This yields uniqueness ('au plus un') of x over i with x≤z, i.e. injectivity of Σ_{≤z} → I_{≤j}. It does not yield existence. Existence/surjectivity would in fact be false: Σ_ij is only a boundary face of Σ_j, so an interior point z of Σ_j has nothing below it. If the marginal word is 'surjectif' (as the transcription reads), it is a slip; the next page indeed speaks of the injection (29) Σ_{*≤z} ↪ I_{≤k}.
The 'cylindrical' hypothesis (collar / product structure near the face) is named but not defined on this page. The parenthetical justification ('par i quelconque…') is incomplete.
Minor: the notation pr_1 = 'but' for the target projection, together with (x,z) with x≤z, is used inconsistently across the two pages.

ideas.what: Encoding the unfolded stratified space as a topological poset Σ_* with closed order graph, fibred over the discrete stratum poset I, with Σ_* = ⊔Σ_i and Σ_** = ⊔Σ_ij.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution/unzipping of a stratified space into a manifold with corners with iterated fibration structure; topological poset over the poset of strata.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Verona (1984, resolution of Thom–Mather spaces); Melrose and Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012, iterated fibration structures); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017, unzipping of conically smooth spaces).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6: the 'théorie des déploiements' is announced programmatically, without these axioms.

ideas.what: Condition (a): the face maps Σ_ij → Σ_j are cylindrical closed embeddings, hence Σ_ii = Σ_i and uniqueness of the lower point over each smaller stratum.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary faces of a manifold with corners/faces with collars (Jänich ⟨n⟩-manifolds, Laures).

ideas.what: Condition (b): the chain spaces Σ(n) decompose over strict flags of I, giving a simplicial space over the nerve of I with pieces Σ_{i_0…i_n}.
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of a topological poset fibred over N(I); flag-indexed strata of the unfolding (cf. exit-path category over a poset).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A) for exit paths over posets.

missed.claim: A compact axiomatization of the 'déploiement' is given as a single topological poset (closed order graph) over the stratum poset I. Its chain spaces split over flags of I, and its face maps are closed cylindrical embeddings. With the next page's transversality conditions, this is a manifold-with-faces/iterated-fibration formalism. It predates Verona and Melrose-style resolutions and resembles AFT's unzipping, but is phrased as a topological order rather than a diagram of manifolds with corners.
missed.quote: Σ(n) = ens des drapeaux stricts de longueur n de Σ … Σ(n) → Drap_n(I) … ⊔ Σ_{i_0…i_n}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Presenting the unfolded space as a topological poset whose nerve fibres over N(I) gives a direct bridge between Grothendieck's tame-topology program and today's exit-path/∞-categorical (Lurie, AFT) treatments of stratified spaces. It is of historical interest; the mathematics is now largely known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a concrete, unpublished axiomatization of the 'déploiement' only sketched in the Esquisse. The content itself (manifolds with corners indexed by flags, iterated fibrations) was later developed independently. It is a notable historical detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: '(2°)' in the left margin is probably '(29)', continuing the numbering from the previous page's item (29).
'il existe un plus un x' should most likely read 'il existe au plus un x' (underlined 'au plus'), consistent with the closed-embedding hypothesis.
The marginal note likely reads 'i.e. Σ_{*≤z} → I_{≤j} injectif' (or is a slip for it), not 'surjectif'.
'connue de continuité' plausibly reads 'comme condition de continuité'.
The bottom-left margin 'remonte condition (b) dans la condition (a)' plausibly reads 'revient à …', i.e. condition (b) is equivalent to/contained in (a).
